The repository states Lemma 5.4 faithfully, in two pieces built on one shared `Result` record. Hypotheses (5.29)-(5.33) appear in essentially literal form, including Λ_log(q) = 1 + |log q|, the Ω_{aν} factor-support condition and the flat remainder E_{J,m} of (5.33). The conclusion is stronger than the paper's on several axes: integer scales, tail bounds for m ≤ J+2 (J+3 for scalars) rather than m ≤ J, an arbitrary Fintype of scalar entries, and the extra (5.40) test weights. The differences are re-encodings: the isotropic replacement of (5.28), the log-free base bound (bridged by base_rate_of_raw_log), and the split of the lemma into construction plus residual flatness. I found nothing stated more weakly than the paper and nothing missing.

findings.summary: No single declaration states Lemma 5.4. The construction with (5.34)/(5.35) is `exists_angular_realization`; the residual conclusion (5.36) is the separate `Result.flat_residual_of_raw_bounds`, which takes that same `Result` as its first argument.
In the tuple version, the base bound on U_0 is assumed without the paper's log factor: `JetRate … u0 m (-K0 m)` rather than C_m q^{-K_m}Λ_log(q)^{P_m}. The repository supplies the conversion itself.

Hypothesis (5.28) is replaced by the isotropic bound ‖D^k q‖ ≤ B_k q^{1-k} over all space-time directions, dropping the anisotropy parameter D. This weakens the hypothesis, so the Lean theorem is the more general one.
